rounds.text: NIIT Ltd trades at a highly attractive price-to-book ratio of just 1.11x (at a share price of ₹ 86.9 against a book value of ₹ 78.5) [E2], which is roughly half of the sector benchmark P/B of 2.22x [E7]. This provides a strong asset-backed margin of safety for investors at a market capitalization of ₹ 1,190 Cr [E3], especially when the business is actively demonstrating a powerful fundamental turnaround. Compounded sales growth has accelerated notably to 5% over 3 years [E16] and 12% over the trailing twelve months [E17], backed by strong screen signals showing recent year-on-year sales growth of 14% [E68] and profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E70]. This operational momentum sits comfortably alongside a solid dividend yield of 1.15% [E4], rewarding patient shareholders while the broader recovery takes root. Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E26], [E27], [E28], [E29].

NIIT Ltd carries an extreme valuation that is completely disconnected from its actual financial returns, trading at a staggering P/E of 84.7 according to filed statements [E1], which balloons even further to 130.22x against a sector benchmark of just 26.2x [E6]. This lofty pricing is severely unsupported by fundamental profitability, as evidenced by a miserable return on equity of 1% over the last year [E29] and a deteriorating 3-year median ROE of just 3% [E28], alongside an anemic ROCE of 2.2% [E12] that drastically underperforms the sector median ROCE of 8.4% [E80]. Furthermore, the business suffers from long-term top-line decay, having delivered a compounded sales growth of -16% over 5 years [E15] and -9% over 10 years [E14], cementing its flag for poor 5-year sales growth of -16.5% [E64]. Speculative expectations are dangerously detached from fundamental delivery, highlighted by the scanX signal engine noting that recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 51% [E58]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated recent top-line momentum with a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 12% [E17] and year-over-year sales growth of 14% [E68].

The bear's alarm over high price-to-earnings multiples [E1, E6] ignores the fact that the company trades at a highly attractive price-to-book of just 1.11x [E2], representing a steep discount to the sector benchmark P/B of 2.22x [E7]. While the bear highlights weak historical returns like a 10-year sales decline [E14] and 5-year sales decay [E15, E64], it understates the powerful operational inflection currently underway, demonstrated by a positive 3-year compounded sales growth of 5% [E16], a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 12% [E17], and year-over-year sales expansion of 14% [E68]. Conceded: historical return on equity is low at 1% over the last year [E29], 3% over 3 years [E28], and 5% over 5 years [E27], alongside an ROCE of 2.2% [E12] that trails the sector [E80]. However, this cyclical trough in returns is already heavily discounted by the modest market capitalization of ₹ 1,190 Cr [E3] and a stock price sitting comfortably at just 61% of its 52-week range [E5], leaving plenty of room for re-rating as recent profit growth exceeding 20% YoY takes hold [E70].

The bull dismisses the staggering P/E multiples of 84.7x and 130.22x by hiding behind a price-to-book ratio of 1.11x [E1, E2, E6], yet ignores that asset cheapness means little when capital is chronically unproductive, proven by a dismal 2.2% ROCE against a sector benchmark of 8.4% [E12, E80]. Conceded: the company displays recent top-line flickers with a 3-year sales growth of 5%, trailing twelve-month sales growth of 12%, and year-over-year sales expansion of 14% [E16, E17, E68], but these short-term metrics arrive on the back of a catastrophic long-term decay featuring a 10-year sales contraction of -9% and a 5-year sales collapse of -16% [E14, E15, E64]. The bull's faith in a cyclical trough is entirely contradicted by a deteriorating trajectory where median return on equity has steadily degraded from 7% over 10 years to 5% over 5 years, 3% over 3 years, and a pathetic 1% over the last year [E26, E27, E28, E29, E72]. Finally, the signal engine flatly exposes that price growth has outstripped profit growth by 51% [E58], proving that speculative expectations are aggressively running ahead of operational delivery rather than being "heavily discounted" by the ₹ 1,190 Cr market capitalization [E3].
